dedupe_keys.name: floodx open access urban flooding experiments

description: Eawag and ETH Zurich document floodX, a controlled urban flash-flood testbed in Wangen an der Aare, Switzerland. Twenty-two floods were generated in a 25-by-25-metre training facility containing a configurable sewer network and a building. A raised 450-cubic-metre reservoir supplied water, while conventional instruments and five surveillance cameras recorded manhole surcharge, surface flow and basement flooding. The public project page links the 2017 ESSD paper and reusable observation packages. Documentation is free to read but has no stated reuse licence; the linked calibration data use CC0-1.0. The repository warns that two radar-velocity series have systematic errors up to 50% and their absolute values must be disregarded. This limitation is material for model validation. The case supports comparison of sensor and video methods and calibration of urban flood simulations. It complements the separate dataset record by documenting the physical experiment and its instrumentation, without claiming city-scale validation.
